reviews.basis: Player_AnimationFrameTable selects this sprite mapping at the stated index after masking the animation accumulator to eight entries.
reviews.reason: Player_AdvanceAnimationFrame masks the accumulator with $1C and indexes the eight longwords of Player_AnimationFrameTable. Its slots 0 through 7 point in order to these eight mapping labels. The identical sentence states only that shared table relationship; it does not infer the appearance of any frame.

reviews.basis: A SharedCombatSpriteAnimation stream names this frame via a signed relative offset; Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame adds that offset to the cursor, and Sprite_RenderObjectList passes the result to Sprite_RenderMapping on its draw path. The suffix records ROM order, not visual identity.
reviews.reason: Each of these 69 mappings occurs as a dc.w Frame-* relative target in src/data/shared_combat_sprite_animations.s. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame adds the signed offset at (a4) to its cursor; the ordinary Sprite_RenderObjectList draw path then calls Sprite_RenderMapping. The three Stage 15 fragment mappings are excluded and have separate evidence.

reviews.basis: Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame reads this ROM-ordered stream as pairs of signed relative mapping offsets and timing or control words; the numeric suffix denotes ROM order, not a visual identity.
reviews.reason: Each of these 33 ROM-ordered animation labels starts with a relative SharedCombatSpriteFrame pointer followed by a timing word. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame reads the paired words, advances by four bytes between records, and follows a relative sequence pointer when the timing word is zero. The former index 30 has its own Counter Force name and is not part of this group.

reviews.basis: The eight-direction SevenForcesRotationFrameTable0 through SevenForcesRotationFrameTable8 pointer sets select this sprite mapping record. The suffix preserves ROM order without assigning a specific form or body part.
reviews.reason: The nine labelled SevenForcesRotationFrameTable0..8 bases collectively contain pointers to all 40 listed mapping labels. Sprite_ApplyMetaspriteEightFrameRotation masks its table offset with $1C, selecting one of eight slots from a descriptor base. Table1 is followed by a second unlabelled eight-pointer run before Table2; the Table1 base cannot select that run with this mask, and no wider reachability is claimed.

reviews.basis: Named Enemy_Projectile animation streams select this sprite mapping; the numeric suffix preserves ROM order without guessing a pose.
reviews.reason: Every listed mapping appears as a dc.w Enemy_ProjectileSpriteMappingNN-* target in one of the ten Enemy_ProjectileAnimation00..09 streams. Anim_UpdateProjectileAnimation selects those streams through Enemy_ProjectileAnimationPointers, and the mapping names claim only ROM order rather than a visual pose. No frame-to-pose identity is inferred.

reviews.basis: Boss_Shellshogun pointer tables or direct assignments select this sprite mapping; the numeric suffix preserves ROM order without guessing a visual pose.
reviews.reason: Six eight-entry Boss_ShellshogunRotationFramesA..F tables select mappings 03..26. The metasprite descriptor directly names mappings 00 and 02, body-frame assignments name 00 and 01, and Boss_ShellshogunRotatingPartFrameTable names 27..29. These static sources account for every listed mapping; numeric suffixes preserve ROM order and do not assert a visual pose.

reviews.basis: WeaponSetup_ControlTypeTextPointers selects this encoded string at the matching TYPE 1--26 display index.
reviews.reason: WeaponSetup_ControlTypeTextPointers contains exactly 26 longwords in label order 01..26. WeaponSetup_RenderSelectedControlType scales WeaponSetupControlIndex by four and reads that table entry. The eight-byte strings share the TYPE prefix and encode the matching decimal index with digit bytes 1=0 through A=9, followed by $FF; single-digit values use a zero spacer. This is a table and byte-format claim, not an inferred visual pose.

reviews.basis: The encoded glyph bytes decode to the exact weapon-setup or control-test label stated by the symbol and are consumed by the setup text renderer.
reviews.reason: These 20 definitions are dc.b text data, not executable entries. Their alphabetic glyph bytes $B..$24 encode A..Z with zero spaces, yielding the named heading, force, mode, status, exit, or control-test label; $2E precedes button glyphs where present. Every record is reached by a lea or dc.l reference in weapon_setup_screen.s, whose text paths call Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped. The two executable entries formerly sharing this sentence are excluded.

reviews.basis: A Stage 12 Teddy Bear animation stream in the same mapping bank references this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Each of the 18 A-R mapping labels is the target of at least one dc.w Mapping-* entry in the adjacent timed animation streams. Every mapping ends with a sprite command whose first word has bit 15 set. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame adds the signed relative target to its cursor. The Stage12_TeddyBearAnimationVariant streams have no proven source caller; this review establishes table membership and record format, not runtime reachability or visual pose.

reviews.basis: One or more entries in the seven-stream Enemy_PhasePatternAnimationBySelector set stores a self-relative pointer to this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_ApplyPhasePatternAnimationSelector indexes the seven entries of Enemy_PhasePatternAnimationBySelector. Across those seven streams, every A-Q mapping is the target of at least one dc.w Mapping-* relative entry; each mapping's final sprite command has bit 15 set in its first word. The common sentence claims table membership and record format, not a visual pose or execution of every selector in every game state.

reviews.basis: One or more of the four streams selected by Enemy_Stage10WaspAnimationMappings stores a self-relative pointer to this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_UpdateStage10WaspAnimation indexes the four longwords of Enemy_Stage10WaspAnimationMappings. Across their four streams, each A-M mapping is targeted by at least one dc.w Mapping-* entry, and every mapping's final sprite command has bit 15 set in its first word. Selector0C is also assigned during defeat conversion. The shared claim establishes exact stream membership and record format, not one exclusive runtime state or a visual pose.

reviews.basis: The named Sharpssteel state or controller loads this byte stream directly into the blade pose-command interpreter.
reviews.reason: All 13 members are dc.b command streams in sharpssteel_blades.s and each is loaded into a1 by a lea in sharpssteel_core.s or sharpssteel_blades.s. The manual-control path calls Boss_SharpssteelRunBladePoseCommands directly; the other named paths enter Boss_SharpssteelUpdateBladeAssembly, which begins with that call. Each stream ends in $FF,$FF or $FF,$FE. This shared basis proves data type and interpreter connection, not the higher-level visual identity of the pose.

reviews.basis: Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes consumes these signed words as a zero-terminated list relative to Gfx_LoadPalettePreservingSharedColor; the named stage or screen is the static pointer owner.
reviews.reason: Each of these 11 records defines one zero-terminated list of dc.w offsets relative to Gfx_LoadPalettePreservingSharedColor and has a named screen, cutscene, or stage configuration pointer in source. Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes reads the signed word, stops at zero, extends it and adds the preserving-loader base before loading the command. ContinueScreenPaletteOffsetLists is excluded because it contains two consecutive lists and only the first has a direct source pointer; its separate address basis states that limit.

reviews.basis: The named battle-state path loads this word stream into the Valkirie pose interpreter; $80xx words publish events and $FFFE/$FFFF terminate or loop.
reviews.reason: Each of these nine named state scripts has a direct lea Script(pc),a1 in valkirie_battle.s followed by a branch or call to Entity_RenderValkirieBattleAnimation, which calls Anim_UpdateValkiriePoseScript. The streams are dc.w words and each ends in $FFFE or $FFFF; the state-4-to-8 stream also has an internal $FFFF. The three airborne variants are excluded: their addresses are first stored in field $41C(a5) and later loaded indirectly, and their former High/Mid/Low names asserted unproved visual height.

reviews.basis: The structural name records exact width and row position without inventing semantics for the overlapping users.
reviews.reason: The twelve members are longwords 1 through 6 at offsets +4 through +$18 in each of two consecutive 32-byte RAM rows. Effect_ApplyTransitionMask starts at TransitionPatternRow0 and TransitionPatternRow1, then performs two post-increment longword reads/writes per row over four DBF iterations, covering elements 0 through 7. Element 0 in each row and element 7 at each boundary have separately specific evidence; the twelve middle records share only the proven physical width and position, not one scene-specific meaning. Results and boss/cutscene code overlay the same addresses.

reviews.basis: Missiray bullet animation streams select this ROM-ordered sprite mapping record; the suffix does not guess a visual transformation stage.
reviews.reason: All eleven mapping definitions are relative dc.w Frame-* targets in the three Missiray bullet sprite-animation streams in shield_viper_and_missiray_mappings.s. Frame00 occurs in both the initial and transform streams; frames 01-04 occur in the looping stream, while frames 05-10 occur in the transform stream. Projectile_InitMissirayBullet installs the initial pointer, Projectile_MissirayBulletTransform installs the transform pointer, and Projectile_MissirayBulletWaitForTransformFrame installs the loop pointer. The shared sentence states membership and ROM-order naming only, not visual transformation stages or actual runtime reach of every frame.

reviews.basis: Named Enemy_Bird animation streams select this sprite mapping; the numeric suffix preserves ROM order without guessing a pose.
reviews.reason: All eleven mappings are relative dc.w Mapping-* targets in Enemy_BirdAnimation00 through 03. Streams 00 and 01 traverse frames 00-06 forward and backward with different delays; streams 02 and 03 use frames 07-10. The four stream pointers are entries of Enemy_BirdAnimationMappings, indexed by Enemy_UpdateBirdAnimation. Every mapping ends in a high-bit sprite command; streams 00-02 loop to themselves with zero delay and stream 03 ends with $FF. This establishes membership and structural interpretation, not visual pose identities or reachability of each selector during gameplay.

reviews.basis: Boss_SniperHoneyviperTentacleDirectionFrames selects this tentacle mapping through one of its eight indexed longword slots; the suffix records mapping ROM order, not a direction or visual pose.
reviews.reason: The sole source references to all eight mapping definitions are the eight dc.l entries of Boss_SniperHoneyviperTentacleDirectionFrames, in slot order 04/03/02/01/00/07/06/05. Boss_SniperHoneyviperUpdateTentaclesAndChainParts loads that table into a1, masks each of two angles with $E0, shifts by three to obtain byte offsets 0 through $1C, and copies the selected longword to the two tentacle part mapping fields $1E8 and $2A8. Each mapping is a one-sprite record with a high-bit first command. This proves table membership and source ownership, not visual direction names or that all eight slots are reached at runtime.

reviews.basis: The named Medusa state loads this word stream through lea Script(pc),a1 before Boss_RenderMedusaPose invokes Boss_UpdateMedusaPoseScript; $FFFE stops the script and $FFFF loops it.
reviews.reason: These seven dc.w command streams each have a direct lea Script(pc),a1 in a Medusa state handler, followed by a call or branch to Boss_RenderMedusaPose, which invokes Boss_UpdateMedusaPoseScript. Each stream ends in $FFFE or $FFFF. The state-A/C and state-10 scripts also have pointer stores for linked objects; the common claim does not assert exclusive direct use. Medusa_PoseFrameData is excluded: initialization stores its base in $35C(a5), and the interpreter adds script offsets to that base. Medusa_InitialPoseChannelValues already has separate evidence showing initial fixed-point values, not delays.

reviews.basis: After appending particle OAM, Player_RenderDeathParticles masks FrameCounter to $1C and selects this ROM-ordered death-sequence mapping through Player_DeathSequenceAnimationFrames for player field 8(a5).
reviews.reason: Player_RenderDeathParticles first fills a scratch OAM buffer by repeatedly calling Player_WriteDeathParticleSprite and calls Sprite_AppendOAMEntries. Only afterward does it shift FrameCounter by two, mask it with $1C, and use the resulting longword offset to write one of these eight mapping pointers into player field 8(a5). The eight dc.l entries in Player_DeathSequenceAnimationFrames point to these records in ROM order. Their art sources are referenced by the mapping records, not by the particle OAM writer; the former DeathParticle mapping/art names conflated the two paths. This review establishes static ownership and selection order, not a visually confirmed death pose.

reviews.basis: A named Sirene state loads this word command stream with lea Script(pc),a1 and enters Boss_RenderSirenePose, which calls Boss_UpdateSirenePoseScript.
reviews.reason: Sirene_State2PoseScript, Sirene_ActivePoseScript, and Sirene_State4And6PoseScript each have direct lea Script(pc),a1 call sites in Sirene state handlers before the shared pose renderer invokes Boss_UpdateSirenePoseScript. They are dc.w command streams ending in $FFFF, $FFFF, and $FFFE respectively. This establishes the direct interpreter path, not a visual pose identity. The three state-14 scripts are excluded because the state stores their pointers through two lookup tables, and the frame-data base at $057D18 is not a command stream.

reviews.basis: Boss_EnterSireneState14 selects this word command record through one of two four-pointer tables and stores it in $71C(a5); Boss_RenderSireneState14 later loads the pointer into a1 for the pose interpreter.
reviews.reason: Sirene_State14PoseScriptSet0 has entries 0/0/2/2 and Set1 has 0/0/1/1. Boss_EnterSireneState14 selects a set from field $54, masks RandomNumberState by $C for longword offsets 0, 4, 8, or 12, and writes the selected pointer to $71C(a5). Boss_RenderSireneState14 later loads it into a1 before Boss_RenderSirenePose. Each script has a first $FFFE stop marker. Script2 contains four additional command words and a second $FFFE after its first stop; no direct symbolic pointer to that tail is known, so reachability of those words is not claimed.

reviews.basis: The DAC descriptor tables encode this 0x8000-byte ROM-aligned PCM bank through its high address byte plus per-sample offsets.
reviews.reason: PCMPart1 through PCMPart8 occupy eight consecutive $8000-byte asset ranges from $098000 to $0D8000, and pcm_samples.s includes each under the matching Sound_PCMBank1..8 label. Sound_PCMSampleDescriptors and Sound_VoiceDACDescriptors encode these bank bases with (Sound_PCMBankN >> $8) followed by per-sample offset/length words. PCMPart9 begins at $0D8000 but has only $1A5E bytes before padding, so its unique evidence correctly excludes it from this uniform-size group. The bank names and format are structural evidence, not identification of individual voice samples.

reviews.basis: Periodic-shot enemy animation streams reference this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: PeriodicShotEnemySpriteAnimationPointers selects Wait, Transition, or Attack streams. Their relative frame references cover all seven mappings: Wait visits 03/00/01/02/04/02/01/00/03, Attack visits 00/05/06/05, and Transition visits 00/05/03. Each of the seven mapping records has nine six-byte sprite entries, with the high bit set on the final entry. The ROM-order suffix does not assert a visual pose or runtime visit to every stream.

reviews.basis: At least one of Midgame_LightningSpriteAnimation00/01/03 selects this ROM-ordered sprite-mapping record through a relative frame offset; neither a visual pose nor multiple sprite pieces is implied.
reviews.reason: Midgame_UpdateRandomLightningEffect masks RandomNumberState with $C and selects one of four animation pointers. Streams 00, 01, and 03 select exactly this seven-record family through relative dc.w frame offsets; stream 02 instead uses records 07-12. Mapping00-06 contain 4/5/4/3/3/2/1 six-byte sprite entries respectively, so the old shared 'composite' claim was false for mapping06. Each record terminates through the high bit on its final sprite entry. The ROM-order suffix does not assert a visual pose.

reviews.basis: Joker's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_JokerMetaspriteDescriptors references all six 0x20-byte tables, directly or with attribute bits in the high address portion. Each contains eight longword sprite-mapping pointers. A/B are forward/reverse A0-A7, C/D are forward/reverse C0-C7, and E/F are forward/reverse E0-E7. This proves the static pointer-table structure and ordered rotation frames, not the visible direction of a particular index.

reviews.basis: Shellshogun's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_ShellshogunMetaspriteDescriptors references all six 0x20-byte tables with packed high-word attributes. Each contains eight longword sprite-mapping pointers: A/B/C descend 26-19, 10-03, and 18-11, while D/E/F ascend 19-26, 03-10, and 11-18. Boss_ShellshogunUpdateSpriteFlip also indexes F directly with an angle-derived offset masked to $1C. The shared basis asserts only descriptor ownership and pointer-table format; no visual orientation is assigned to a particular index.

reviews.basis: Boss_ZLeoValkirieForceSharedMetaspriteData embeds this exact mapping pointer in its part descriptors; the table is statically shared by both initializers.
reviews.reason: The 16-longword descriptor run at $0355A4 contains three zero entries, one Z-Leo blade mapping, and pointers to all five reviewed mappings: A/B/C three times each, D twice, E once. Boss_ZLeoIntroInit passes that run as a0 to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts with separate radii and links at a1/a2. Boss_ValkirieForceInit passes the same base as a0/a1/a2, so its non-descriptor inputs reinterpret these bytes; static shared address does not prove identical runtime use of each mapping. The five records contain 4/2/1/1/2 six-byte sprite pieces in A/B/C/D/E order, each high-bit-terminated. The suffixes distinguish descriptor targets, not visual identity or ROM order.

reviews.basis: Enemy behavior animation streams reference this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Both Enemy_BehaviorWaitSpriteAnimation and Enemy_BehaviorGroundedSpriteAnimation reference mappings 00-04 in order; the wait stream then reverses through 03-01, and the grounded stream repeats 04 before reversing to 00. The attack-cooldown stream also references mapping 00. The five records contain 5/4/4/6/6 six-byte sprite pieces in ROM order; only the final piece in each carries the terminator bit. These references establish stream membership and composite format, not a visual pose identity.

reviews.basis: Enemy_CirclingLoopAnimation stores a self-relative pointer to this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_CirclingAnimationMappings points to Enemy_CirclingLoopAnimation. That stream names mappings A-E in order with duration 2 after each and ends with a self-relative loop pointer and zero control word. All five mapping records consist of one six-byte piece with its terminator bit set. The adjacent rotation mappings belong to another selector, and A-E asserts sequence membership rather than visible facing.

reviews.basis: Player_WeaponAnimationFrames selects this sprite mapping at the stated weapon-animation index.
reviews.reason: Player_SetWeaponAnimationData uses the frame offset in d1 to read Player_WeaponAnimationFrames. The six longword slots name mappings 00-04 in index order, followed by the distinct Player_DashSecondarySpriteMapping; the reviewed set covers only the five Player_WeaponAnimationSpriteMapping records. Player_UpdateWeaponAnim advances its offset by four and wraps at $18. The suffixes are table indices, not the order of every player pose in ROM or a visual weapon identity.

reviews.basis: Player_PrimaryAnimationLayoutTable contains this sprite mapping at the stated index and Player_PrepareSpriteRendering selects it through the terrain animation-index tables.
reviews.reason: Player_PrepareSpriteRendering installs Player_PrimaryAnimationLayoutTable and Player_PrepareSpriteRendering_WithTables selects a longword through either terrain animation-index table; their entries are multiples of four from 0 through $10. The table lists mappings 00-04 in index order, then separate offset bytes. The mapping records occur in ROM order 04/03/00/02/01, so suffixes state table index rather than physical order or visual pose.

reviews.basis: Player_AlternateAnimationLayoutTable contains this sprite mapping at the stated index and the alternate rendering path selects it through the terrain animation-index tables.
reviews.reason: Alternate player rendering paths pass Player_AlternateAnimationLayoutTable in a0 to Player_PrepareSpriteRendering_WithTables, which uses the same lower/upper terrain index tables as the primary path. Its five longword slots list mappings 00-04 in index order, followed by separate offset bytes. The mapping records instead occur in ROM order 04/03/00/02/01; suffixes state table index, not physical order or a visible pose.

reviews.basis: The routine loads its adjacent descriptor into a0 and tail-calls Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns.
reviews.reason: The three $053A3A/$053A52/$053A6A wrappers each load the matching adjacent MissirayTileTransferSet00/01/02Descriptor into a0, execute nop, then tail-jump to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns. Set 03 instead belongs to a wait-state routine and is not a member. The suffixes identify matching descriptor slots, not a guessed visual tile effect.

reviews.basis: The adjacent Missiray loader passes this word record in a0 to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns.
reviews.reason: Wrappers 00-02 and the set-03 wait state each load their matching descriptor address into a0 before tail-jumping to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns. Sets 00-02 have six words headed by $6020/$2000/$0102; set 03 has five words headed by $6020/$2000/$0101. Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns reads bytes 4 and 5 as loop counts, so a uniform six-word claim would be false. Set 03 has no separate named loader.

reviews.basis: The routine passes its adjacent indexed-row descriptor directly to Tilemap_QueueIndexedRows.
reviews.reason: Each reviewed wrapper loads its adjacent indexed-row descriptor into a0, executes nop, and tail-jumps to Tilemap_QueueIndexedRows: sets 00, 02, 03, 04 and 05. Set 01 instead falls through to a shared jump tail; set 06 is embedded in the rise-state threshold path. Their exclusion is deliberate. The five descriptor bodies are seven words each, but carry different destination/index words and are not assumed to show the same tiles.

reviews.basis: Direct references from the options/frontend renderer establish the table's consumer and displayed role.
reviews.reason: UI_UpdateMessageOption, UI_UpdateBGMOption and UI_UpdateSFXOption pass On as a1 and Off as a2; UI_UpdateDifficultyOption passes SuperEasy as a1 and SuperHard as a2. Options_ApplyToggleAndQueueLabels copies each choice only until its first $FFFF word. The exact first-string lengths are 4/3/10/9 tile words in On/Off/SuperEasy/SuperHard order. Two additional terminated strings follow SuperHard in ROM but are outside this direct reader's first string; no visual or reachability claim is made for them.

reviews.basis: The type-$410 Stage 24 object's relative-offset animation selects this sprite mapping record; the frame suffix preserves ROM order.
reviews.reason: StageTransition_InitializeStage24SceneObjects assigns type $410 to Entity57; slot $410/4 of Entity_UpdateHandlerTable dispatches its Stage24SceneObject states, and HoldExpandedFrame installs Stage24SceneObject_SpriteAnimation in field 8. The animation lists the five reviewed mapping labels as consecutive Frame01-Frame05 relative offsets after Frame00, with timing words 8/8/9/8/8; Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame resolves such offsets for Sprite_RenderObjectList. The suffix follows ROM and stream order, not an inferred appearance.

reviews.basis: Antroid's secondary descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: The secondary Antroid metasprite descriptor array includes D/F/E/G at slots 0/2/7/9, each with the +1 inline-descriptor marker. At $03499E/$0349A4/$0349AA/$0349B0, each target contains exactly three dc.w fields before the next label. Boss_AntroidInitializeBattleState passes this array to Sprite_InitializeAdditionalLinkedMetaspriteParts, whose low-bit branch handles inline descriptors. The letters encode ROM order, not visual identity.

reviews.basis: Back Stringer's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Back Stringer's linked-part initializer receives Boss_BackStringerMetaspriteDescriptors. That descriptor list references each A-D rotation table, with repeated C/A/D/B slots and attribute flags; the common metasprite initializer follows its rotation-frame branch. Each table holds eight dc.l mapping pointers. A/B traverse set A in opposite orders, and C/D traverse set C in opposite orders. No on-screen direction is assigned to any suffix.

reviews.basis: Madam Barbar's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Madam Barbar's setup passes Boss_MadamBarbarMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts. That descriptor list references each A-D rotation table, sometimes with high-bit attribute flags; the initializer's rotation-frame branch handles them. Each table holds eight dc.l mapping pointers. B reverses A's set-A order, while C/D traverse set B in ascending/descending order. No on-screen direction is assigned to any suffix.

reviews.basis: The frames before that timer expires return here.
reviews.reason: All four Phase Pattern states start by decrementing $48(a5) and use bne.s to reach their own return label while the countdown is nonzero. At zero, each performs its distinct state/animation/motion update and falls through to the same RTS: WaitBeforeAttack selects $14 and state +2; BeginHorizontalMotion selects $1C and sets $18 to -1; StopHorizontalMotion clears $18 and selects $18; Restart restores the $100 wait, animation 4, and state 2. The shared sentence covers only the nonzero-countdown branch, not identical expiry effects.

reviews.basis: The three shared projectile streams reference this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping and differ only in their per-frame durations.
reviews.reason: SharedProjectileDuration2/4/8Animation each lists mappings A-D in the same order, with timing words 2/4/8 respectively for the first three frames and $FF after the fourth. Each mapping is one three-word sprite command whose first word has bit 15 set. Boss_SnakeShotMappingChoices references all three streams; duration 4 also has direct installs in Stage 12, Gusthead, shared directional volley, and bouncing-object code. The older blanket Stage 18 direct-consumer claim has no matching symbolic install in the current source and is not retained. Letters encode ROM order, not visible poses.

reviews.basis: Xi-Tiger's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_XiTigerSetup passes Boss_XiTigerMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts, whose rotation-frame branch stores the table pointer. That descriptor list references all four A-D tables, sometimes with high-bit attributes. Each table holds eight longword mapping pointers: A and C traverse Xi-Tiger rotation set A in ascending and descending order, while B and D do the same for set B. The suffixes record ROM order, not a visual direction.

reviews.basis: The wrapper supplies D7 value eighteen and the shared interpolation workspace to Anim_InitializePoseChannelsFromBytes.
reviews.reason: Each of the four reviewed wrappers executes moveq #$12,d7, points a1 at SharedPatternRow0Long0, and tail-jumps to Anim_InitializePoseChannelsFromBytes with source bytes in a0. The shared routine writes one shifted word and one zero-delta word per source byte, then dbf d7 repeats: an initial $12 means nineteen channels. One original Valkirie viewer wrapper instead passes $10 and is deliberately not included.

reviews.basis: A stage-specific initializer or graphics path selects this exact 30-byte record address before Stage_ApplyConfigurationRecord consumes its fixed fields and palette-list pointer.
reviews.reason: Stage_InitializerOffsets selects Stage_ApplyStage1Configuration, Stage_ApplyStage2Configuration, and Stage_InitializeStage8 at StageTableIndex offsets $00, $02, and $0E. Each wrapper loads its corresponding record into A0 and reaches Stage_ApplyConfigurationRecord, which consumes 30 bytes in the declared field order and passes the final palette-list pointer to Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes. These are three exact records, not evidence that every stage initializer has identical side effects: Stage 8 also initializes tilemap ranges.

reviews.basis: Only the adjacent unreferenced Stage 20 variant wrapper selects this 30-byte record.
reviews.reason: The four consecutive 30-byte records start with distinct StageStateOffset values $28/$30/$38/$40 and share the same palette offset list. Each is loaded by the adjacent matching variant wrapper, then passed to Stage_ApplyConfigurationRecord; the wrappers also fill four tilemap word ranges. None of these wrappers appears in Stage_InitializerOffsets, whose Stage 20 slot selects Stage_InitializeStage20 and its separate Stage20ConfigRecord. 'Unreferenced' is limited to the current source-level static call/dispatch graph, not a proof of runtime unreachability via indirect pointers.
